blocks.text: Al. Syro, or suo. Hyginus, Fab. 197: the Syrians regard fish and doves as among the gods; they do not eat them. Lucian, in the place cited above, on the Hierapolitans: Ὀρνίθων τε αὐτέοισι περιστερὴ δοκέει χρῆμα ἱρώτατον, καὶ οὐδὲ ψαύειν αὐτέων δικαιεῦσι· [Ornithōn te auteoisi peristerē dokeei chrēma hirōtaton, kai oude psauein auteōn dikaieusi] Among birds the dove seems to them the most sacred, and they do not think it right even to touch it. Likewise: Ὄρνιθας τοὺς μὲν ἄλλους σιτέονται· περιστερὴν δὲ μούνην οὐ σιτέονται, ἀλλὰ σφίσι ἥδε ἱερή. [Ornithas tous men allous siteontai; peristerēn de mounēn ou siteontai, alla sphisi hēde hierē] [col. 6] They eat other birds, but abstain from the dove alone, which is sacred to them. Phornutus, in the book On the Gods, in the chapter on Rhea: Ἔοικε δὲ ἡ αὐτὴ ἡ παρὰ Σύροις Ἄρταγα εἶναι, ἣν διὰ τὸ περιστερὰς καὶ ἰχθύος ἀπέχεσθαι τιμῶσι· [Eoike de hē autē hē para Syrois Artaga einai, hēn dia to peristeras kai ichthyos apechesthai timōsi] She seems to be the same as the one whom the Syrians call Artaga (others Atergatis and Derceto) and whom they worship by abstaining from fish and the dove. Clement of Alexandria in the Protrepticus: Οὐδέ γε τῶν τὴν Φοινίκην Σύρων κατοικούντων (ἐκλήσομαι) ὧν οἱ μὲν τὰς περιστερὰς, οἱ δὲ τοὺς ἰχθῦς οὕτω σέβουσι περιττῶς, ὡς Ἠλεῖοι τὸν Δία· [Oude ge tōn tēn Phoinikēn Syrōn katoikountōn (eklēsomai) hōn hoi men tas peristeras, hoi de tous ichthys houtō sebousi perittōs, hōs Ēleioi ton Dia] Nor shall I forget the Syrians who live in Phoenicia, some of whom worship doves, others fish, as fervently as the Eleans worship Jupiter. Meor enajim: ונמצאו קצת אמות שבכה אהבו את זכר סמיראמיס ואות דגלה שאסרו על עצמן לאכול את בני היונה And certain nations were found who so revered the memory of Semiramis and the [II, 530] emblem of her banner that they forbade themselves to eat doves. Nor were the Samaritans free from this superstition, if indeed we believe the Jews. The Talmud, tractate Cholin, ch. 1, fol. 6a, on the Cuthaeans or Samaritans: אמר רב נחמן בר יצחק דמות יונה מצאו להן בראש הר גריזים שהיו עובדין אותה Said Rab Nachman, son of Isaac: they found among them the image of a dove, which they worshipped on Mount Gerizim. The gloss on the Talmudic tractate Avodazera, fol. 26b: אל ימול כותי שמל לשם דמות שנמצאו בראש הר גריזים ועובדין לה עבודה כדאמר בהכל שיחטין ומלו את בניהם לשם יונה זו, A Cuthaean shall not circumcise, for he circumcises in the name of the image which they found on the summit of Mount Gerizim, and they worship it, as is related in the chapter (of Cholin, cited above, which begins) "All slaughter": and they circumcise their sons in the name of this dove. Meor enajim: קרוב בעיני להאמין שהכותיים אשר הושיב מלך אשור ובבל בשומרון לאות ולעד הכנעם באהבה אל מלכם ההוא אשר אות דגלה יונה חבבו אותה והקימוהו ליראתם בראש הר גריזים אשר עם שכם ראש ממלכת שומרון בימים ההם, I am fully persuaded that the Cuthaeans, whom the king of Assyria and Babylonia had deported to Samaria, as a sign and testimony of their love and devotion toward their king, who had the dove as the emblem of his banner, loved the dove, and erected a statue, which they worshipped, on the summit of Mount Gerizim, near the city of Shechem, which was then the capital of the Samaritan kingdom. Tsemach David, in the Chronology of the Second Temple, at the year 881: In the days of R. Meir they found the Cuthaeans' image of a dove on Mount Gerizim, as is stated in the first chapter of Cholin. And he decreed that they should be treated in every respect as gentiles of the land. ^{(1)}.
